title: Best Ways to Get Roofing Jobs | Roofr
summary: Looking for the best way to get roofing jobs? Boost your roofing business this busy season by improving your process, speed to lead, and customer experience.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


Want to win more roofing jobs? Recklessly scaling up your marketing isn't the way. First, focus on quality of service, customer communication, and process. It drives referrals and real ROI. Once you have those locked down, THEN marketing can help you scale. Read on for specifics to help you build your game plan.


Never mind 2026, we're already falling into 2027. Is your roofing business ready?


North America's roofing industry is still growing and innovating. But with that comes increased competition. To succeed, it’s not just about marketing harder or shouting louder. Perfecting your process, responding faster, and building lasting relationships with your community will make the true difference.


The best way to get more roofing jobs depends on your business, your location, and your target customers. But if you read and follow the best practices in this article, you'll position your roofing company for success in the coming year.


We'll cover everything from making the right impression to proper follow-up, and from interpreting (and acting on) data to making your whole process smoother and more efficient.


Let’s dive in and set you up to sell more roofs this busy season.


## Be professional and consistent


If you expect customers to choose you over another roofing company, you need to both stand out and impress. Every point of contact you make is a chance to be memorable and leave an impression on a homeowner.


Do you have a logo? Is that logo on your website, emails, Facebook page, proposals, and invoices?


Does all your marketing material use the same fonts and colours?


The real question: Could your past and current customers recognize your business from a lineup?


In roofing, you've gotta be recognizable. Consistency is key. It shows homeowners you're a professional business they can trust.


If you don't have your branding nailed down yet, take time now to get these foundations solidified. It's a necessity in the long run.


## Build your brand and reputation


Your brand is more than just a logo: it’s your reputation. Roofing is a trust-based business, and a strong reputation WILL make all the difference.


It takes work, but a lasting roofing business will:


- Engage with their local community through sponsorships or partnerships.
- Encourage happy customers to leave online reviews.
- Share their expertise through blog posts, social media, or community workshops.


A well-managed reputation both wins new jobs and keeps customers coming back for future projects.


## Marketing isn’t enough: It’s about speed


While[marketing gets you leads](https://roofr.com/gated-content/roofers-marketing-guide) , winning the job depends on how you handle them. And if your reputation is sunk, then marketing won't save you.


Treating new leads right is the best way to kickstart new customer relationships on the right foot.


**Speed to lead** — the time it takes for you to respond to a potential customer — is one of the most critical factors.[If you can respond to leads within 5 minutes](https://www.callpage.io/blog/posts/speed-to-lead) , the conversion rate sits around 70%. That drops to 50% at 30 minutes, and then to 5% at 24 hours.


5 minutes may seem impossible, but a smart process combined with the right roofing software makes it entirely doable. If you're in a competitive market, it's a necessity.


Speed is a great start, but then make sure you back it up with quality: friendly customer service, good value, and commitment to workmanship. Customers need to see why you’re the best choice. This is where professional proposals, clear communication, and stellar reviews come in.


**The right roofing CRM can and will help with this too.** It doesn't *need* to be Roofr, but since it's[completely free to make an account](https://app.roofr.com/register) and test the software out, you're doing yourself a disservice if you don't at least try it out.


## Set a process: Follow up after every job


Another big factor on customer experience — and referrals and reputation — is how you treat your customers during and after production.


Do you leave their lawn free of debris? Do you reach out for a review after? Is your installation crew kind to them?


Your production and post-production process is very important. Too many roofing companies stop thinking about the process after the sale. In doing so, you're losing out on huge potential future sales.


['Better follow-up' was the #1 missed opportunity homeowners identified after a roofing job](https://roofr.com/gated-content/homeowner-report-2026) . 74% of homeowners say responsiveness and communication matter more than price. So be friendly, follow up, and make sure homeowners feel taken care of.


## Be the reliable go-to roofer in your neighborhood


People like to work with businesses they know and trust. Becoming the[go-to roofer in your neighborhood](https://roofr.com/blog/neighborhood-roofer-explained) requires more than just great work. It means showing up, being visible, and actually giving a damn.


In the[Roofr Report podcast](https://roofr.com/podcasts) , we often discuss strategies for building local connections, from leveraging neighborhood networks to creating personalized marketing campaigns. By positioning yourself as a trusted local expert, you’ll not only win more jobs but also build long-term customer relationships.


You can grow your reputation as the neighborhood roofer by:


- Participating in local events
- Being active in community facebook groups
- Using lawn signs and door hangers
- Donating to local charities
- Sponsoring local groups or sports teams


Show up!


## Understand your market and your audience


Every market is different. To succeed, you need to understand the specific needs and preferences of your local audience. Here are some tips:


- Survey past customers to identify what matters most to them.
- Research competitors to see what strategies work in your area.
- Use tools like Google Trends to spot regional roofing trends.


This knowledge allows you to tailor your services and marketing efforts to what your audience values most, helping you stand out.


## Sell the way your customers want to buy


[Different generations have different buying preferences](https://roofr.com/gated-content/selling-roofing-to-each-generation) . To sell more, you need to adapt your sales approach to your audience:


- **Millennials and Gen Z:** These tech-savvy customers prefer digital communication like texting, email, and online booking.
- **Gen X and Baby Boomers:** While they may appreciate digital tools, many still value personal interactions and clear, face-to-face communication.


By understanding how your customers want to buy, you can tailor your sales process to meet their expectations, increasing your chances of closing the deal.


## Software: Your sidekick in roofing sales


Software encompasses a whole lot of tools, all of which can help you sell more. By implementing tech into your entire sales process, you can remove pain points for your business, improve your sales strategy, and help your team close more deals.


### Improved speed to lead


Remember what we said about speed to lead? Automation tools can handle time-consuming tasks like sending follow-up emails, scheduling appointments, or generating initial quotes.


For example, Roofr’s[Instant Estimator](https://roofr.com/estimator) lets you provide potential customers with ballpark pricing immediately, so you never lose a lead to a faster competitor.


The automation triggers in the CRM mean that when a new lead comes in, they get an email right away! That speedy response time will make you stand out from the competition.


### Long-lasting impressions to drive referrals


Additionally, using software can help you build positive impressions that will last long after the job is complete. We know that referrals are huge in roofing, and they're only going to come from satisfied customers.


Winning more sales depends on a world-class customer service, building trust, listening to customers, and focusing on long-term relationship building.


Software that can help you make easy-to-read proposals, simplify customer communication, and an easy payment process post job can make all the difference to a homeowner.


### Measure what works with data


Are you pouring money into marketing without knowing which efforts lead to sales? Tracking data is the key to understanding what works — and what doesn’t. By analyzing metrics like lead conversion rates, proposal acceptance, and response times, you can identify areas for improvement and allocate your resources more effectively.


If you really want to increase roofing sales, then you need to focus in on what actually sells you roofs. There's no point spending hours every week door knocking, for example, if it doesn't actually bring you business.


## Best ways to get roofing jobs: Key takeaways


- Don't blindly focus on marketing. It doesn't matter how much you spend on ads if your customer experience is bad.
- Creating a world-class customer experience will grow your reputation and drive referrals.
- Make sure you know your target homeowners: Are they newer home buyers? Younger? Older?
- [Sell to homeowners the way they want to be sold to](https://roofr.com/gated-content/selling-roofing-to-each-generation) .
- Use software to improve your speed to lead, customer experience, and sales process.
- Track what actually sells so you can focus your efforts in a smart way.


## Set yourself up for success in 2027


Winning roofing jobs means working smarter, not harder. By focusing on speed, leveraging data, and investing in tools that streamline your operations, you can stay ahead of the competition and deliver an exceptional customer experience.
